# Read a page with `web_fetch`

`web_fetch` reads one public HTTP or HTTPS URL through the SerpApi Extract API. Use it to read a page found by `web_search`.

```python
from serpapi_search_tools import web_fetch

fetch = web_fetch(provider="function")
markdown = fetch(url="https://example.com")
print(markdown)
```

The agent supplies only `url`. The tool uses `engine="extract"` and `mode="scrape"`. It does not execute JavaScript. Use [`web_map`](web_map.html) to discover URLs or [`web_crawl`](web_crawl.html) to read linked pages.

## Response modes

Markdown output preserves the API response, including whitespace, headings, and links. For ordinary pages it contains the page content. If a Google or Bing search URL redirects to its dedicated engine, it can contain search results and metadata instead.

| Configuration | Returned value |
| --- | --- |
| Default, or any Markdown configuration | The API's `output=md` response unchanged |
| `response_format="json"` | A JSON string containing only `{"markdown":"..."}` |
| `mode="full", response_format="json"` | The complete JSON response |

Compact JSON raises `SerpApiSearchError` if the response has a missing or empty `markdown` field. Use full JSON to read the available metadata, structured page fields, or a redirected engine's response. To omit Markdown from full JSON, set `default_params={"include_markdown": False}`.

## Configure extraction

```python
from serpapi_search_tools import web_fetch

fetch = web_fetch(
    provider="function",
    timeout=90,
    default_params={
        "include_tags": "main,article",
        "exclude_tags": "nav,footer,.ads",
        "timeout": 30000,
    },
)
```

The constructor's `timeout` controls the SDK request in seconds. `default_params["timeout"]` controls the Extract API's page fetch in milliseconds. Other settings include `device`, `prefetch_delay`, and `no_cache`.

See [Common configuration](configuration.html) for provider and client options and the [Extract API reference](https://serpapi.com/extract-api) for supported page filters.
